children: U.S. industrial production was unchanged between August and July, according to data published by the Federal Reserve.
Production held flat last month after rising in July and June. Analysts polled by The Wall Street Journal expected a 0.3% increase.
Manufacturing output fell 0.3% in August following seven consecutive months of gains.

Production of durable goods was down 0.5%, with broad-based declines across categories. Nondurable production was unchanged month-over-month. Output from utilities jumped 1.8%, and the index for mining output ticked up 0.1%.
Industrial capacity utilization held steady at 76.3% in August, a tick below estimates and 3.1 percentage points below its long-run average.
